notes:
The sheet is drawn rotated about 39 deg CW; it was traced on a de-rotated copy (image rotated +38.6 deg) and every junction was then re-checked at native resolution. Electrically it is a three-rail ladder: a top rail, a middle rail (which carries both GND symbols) and a bottom rail, joined by five vertical rungs. In the description below "top/middle/bottom" and "left/right" are in the de-rotated (electrical) orientation.
Net map: 0 = the ground reference. It is the LEFT segment of the middle rail (from GND 14 at the far left, through the crossings with rung 1 and rung 2, to the left plate of cap 12) plus, via GND 4, the bottom lead of R16 - GND 14 and GND 4 are drawn at opposite ends of the sheet but are one reference, so both and everything on the left middle-rail segment are net "0". Terminals on 0: lower lead of V-AC 0, upper lead of I-DC 1, lower lead of zener 17, upper lead of diode 9, left plate of cap 12, R16 bottom, GND 14, GND 4. n1 = the short link between V-AC 0 and inductor 10 (see the off-frame note below). n2 = top rail LEFT segment: right lead of inductor 10, top of zener 17 (rung 2), top of diode 18 (rung 3), left plate of cap 13. n3 = top rail RIGHT segment: right plate of cap 13, top of zener 3 (rung 4), top of diode 6 (rung 5). n4 = middle rail CENTRE segment: right plate of cap 12, bottom of diode 18, top of zener 2, bottom of zener 3, top of diode 11, left lead of inductor 7. n5 = middle rail RIGHT segment: right lead of inductor 7, bottom of diode 6, top of diode 5, top of R16. n6 = bottom rail LEFT segment: lower lead of I-DC 1 and left plate of cap 15 (the corner between them is at orig (5.8,146), hard against the left frame edge, and is a clean corner with nothing continuing off-frame). n7 = bottom rail CENTRE segment: right plate of cap 15, bottom of diode 9, bottom of zener 2, left lead of inductor 8. n8 = bottom rail RIGHT segment: right lead of inductor 8, bottom of diode 11, bottom of diode 5.
Judgment calls: (a) OFF-FRAME / CUT-OFF COMPONENTS - V-AC 0 (bbox centre orig (107.6,30)) and Inductor 10 (centre orig (176,31.6)) have essentially no ink in the image: the picture contains NO dark pixel anywhere above y=43, so the whole top band of the drawing was lost by the preprocessing crop, and both symbols sit in that band. What survives is (i) the top of rung 1 running up-right from the middle rail and stopping at orig (121.8,42.7) after a small downward arc at orig (98..122, 42..49) - that arc is the visible bottom of V-AC 0's circle, which is centred right there - and (ii) the top rail's left end, which simply begins at orig (194,42) with no corner. Those are the only two open wire ends near the cut, and exactly two components are missing, so they were paired in the order their bboxes give: rung 1 -> V-AC 0 -> (corner, off-frame) -> inductor 10 -> top rail left segment. V-AC 0's centre lies on rung 1 above the middle rail and inductor 10's centre lies on the top rail just left of its visible start, which fixes the order. n1 is the (invisible) node between them. Neither component is marked unconnected - the leads exist, the crop just removed them. (b) All five rungs cross the middle rail as plain X's with only the slight thickening two crossing pen strokes always give - no drawn dot and no hop anywhere on the sheet. They are read as JUNCTIONS, because the alternative (crossings) splits the drawing into two electrically disconnected pieces: the middle rail (GND 14 - cap 12 - inductor 7 - R16 - GND 4) would become an isolated grounded loop and the rest of the ladder would have no reference at all. This is the reading that makes the circuit function, and it is the only one consistent with a ladder. (c) Tier 2, kept deliberately: net n6 (the bottom-left corner between I-DC 1 and cap 15) has NO DC path to ground, because its only two elements are a current source and a capacitor, both open at DC. The ink is unambiguous - I-DC 1 is the "3A" source in rung 1, cap 15 is the "1uF" on the bottom rail, and the corner joining them at orig (5.8,146) is clean - so this is a real property of the drawing (a normal situation for an AC problem), not a mis-trace. simcheck reports it as "net 'n6' has NO DC PATH TO GROUND"; there is no Tier 1 fault (n6 has two terminals, so the current source is not left without a return, and nothing is islanded). (d) 2-terminal parts are stored top-then-bottom for the rung elements and left-then-right for the rail elements, as drawn in the de-rotated frame; that order does not affect any metric. (e) Component inventory unchanged: nothing added, removed or re-classed.
